# nexus machine restart

Reboot the host

Reboots the host nexusd runs on (systemctl reboot on systemd, /sbin/reboot on OpenRC). Side effects: every service on the host, nexusd included, is down for the length of a boot. Guards, all checked before any operation exists, in this order: confirmHost must equal the host's name as system.capabilities.get reports it, exactly (else 400 validation-failed); providers.services.reboot.enabled must be true in the file on the host and the reboot available here (else 409 reboot-unavailable); nexusd must be enabled at boot so the API comes back (else 409 nexusd-not-enabled-at-boot); no other operation may be queued or running (else 409 operations-running with their IDs; force true skips this guard only, and is audited); the configuration must be valid so nexusd starts after the boot (else 422 config-invalid). The guards run again when the operation starts. The reboot is triggered delaySeconds (default 10, 5 to 300) after the operation is recorded; a cancel during the delay ends it Canceled with nothing sent, and a cancel once the reboot is requested answers 409 not-cancelable. The operation completes in the next boot: Succeeded with previousBootId, bootId, upAt, the kernel releases and the reboot-required state, or Failed reboot-did-not-happen when the trigger failed or the host did not go down within providers.services.reboot.timeout. whatIf true runs every guard, reports each with the boot ID, uptime, reboot-required state, running operations and whether nexusd is enabled at boot, and reboots nothing. Long-running: answers 202 with an operation ID; one reboot at a time. REST and CLI only (nexus machine restart): not an MCP tool.

## Usage

```
nexus machine restart [flags]
```

## Examples

```
  # Reboot the host
  nexus machine restart
  # The same, safe to retry
  nexus machine restart --idempotency-key <key>
```

## Flags

```
      --confirm-host string      The host's name exactly as system.capabilities.get reports it, typed by the operator.
      --delay-seconds int        Seconds between the operation being recorded and the reboot, 5 to 300. Default 10.
      --filter stringArray       key=value, repeatable: print only objects whose dot path has this value; a repeated key matches any of its values
      --follow                   stream the operation's output to stderr while waiting
      --force                    Reboot even though other operations are queued or running. Skips that guard only; audited.
  -h, --help                     help for restart
      --idempotency-key string   Idempotency-Key header: a retry with the same key and input returns the original operation (at most 255 visible ASCII characters)
      --no-wait                  print the operation as accepted and exit, without waiting for it to end
  -o, --output string            output format: table, json, jsonl, yaml (default table on a terminal, jsonl otherwise)
      --select strings           print only these dot paths of each object, comma-separated, such as name,properties.state; host and id are always kept
      --tag strings              target every configured host with this tag; comma-separated or repeated for any of several
      --timeout duration         stop waiting after this long, such as 90s or 5m, and exit 7; the operation is not canceled
      --what-if                  Run every guard and report them, and reboot nothing.
      --yes                      no y/N question is asked here; --yes neither fills nor skips --confirm-host, which is required without a terminal
```

## Global flags

```
      --host string   target hosts: configured names, comma-separated, or all (default: NEXUS_HOST, then the default host)
      --verbose       log each request and response status to stderr
```
